content: The drug chamber is filled with cefotixin sodium USP, a semi-synthetic, broad-spectrum cephalosporin antibiotic, sealed under nitrogen for intravenous administration. It is derived from cephamycin C, which is produced by Streptomyces lactamdurans. The chemical name of cefotixin sodium is sodium (6R,7S)-3-(hydroxymethyl)-7-methoxy-8-oxo-7-[2-(thiophene-2-carbonylamino)acetamido]-5-thia-1-azabicyclo[4.2.0]oct-2-ene-2-carboxylate. Each gram of cefotixin activity contains 44.3 mEq of sodium. Cefotixin for Injection and Dextrose Injection is provided as a sterile, non-pyrogenic, single-use packaged combination of cefotixin (prepared using Cefotixin Sodium USP) and Dextrose Injection (as the diluent). After reconstitution, each 50 mL contains cefotixin sodium equivalent to either 1 gram or 2 grams of cefotixin. The diluent chamber contains Dextrose Injection, and the concentration of Dextrose Hydrous USP in Water for Injection USP has been adjusted to make the reconstituted drug product iso-osmotic. The final concentration of dextrose is 2% w/v for both the 1 g and 2 g doses. Dextrose Injection is sterile, non-pyrogenic, and does not contain any bacteriostatic or antimicrobial agents. After removing the peelable foil strip, activating the seals, and thoroughly mixing, the reconstituted drug product is intended for single intravenous use. When reconstituted according to the instructions provided in the product labeling, the approximate osmolality of the reconstituted solution of Cefotixin for Injection and Dextrose Injection is approximately 290 mOsmol/kg. The solutions of Cefotixin for Injection and Dextrose Injection range in appearance from colorless to light amber. The product is not made with natural rubber latex, PVC, or di(2-ethylhexyl)phthalate (DEHP). The DUPLEX® dual chamber container is constructed from a specially formulated material. The contact layer of the product (both diluent and drug) is composed of a mixture of thermoplastic rubber and a polypropylene-ethylene copolymer, which does not contain plasticizers. The safety of the container system is supported by USP biological evaluation procedures.
